{{Recipe summary
| Category = American recipes
| Servings = 10
| Difficulty = 2
}}

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Texas cuisine|Texas Cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Tex-Mex cuisine|Tex-Mex Cuisine]]

==Ingredients==
*1 [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]] (450 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) dry [[Cookbook:Pinto Bean|pinto beans]]
*8 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] water
*1 ½ [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Paprika|paprika]] OR ½ tsp each of paprika and [[Cookbook:Pepper|pepper]]
*1 ½ tbsp granulated or brown [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
*1 tbsp salt OR 2 tsp salt and a ham hock
*1 ½ tbsp [[Cookbook:Chili Powder|chili powder]]
*¼ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] (or more) [[Cookbook:Garlic Powder|garlic powder]]	
*1 ½ tbsp dehydrated [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]] OR ½ small onion, finely [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]]
*1–2 [[Cookbook:Bay leaf|bay leaves]]
*5 cups water

==Procedure==
#Wash beans carefully and [[Cookbook:Soaking Beans|soak]] overnight in 8 cups of water.  
#Drain and refill with 5 cups of water.  
#Add all the other ingredients. 
#Bring to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]] and [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] at least an hour, or until tender.  
#Remove bay leaves.  
#Do not drain prior to serving, as the liquid is an important aspect of the dish. It can be served using slotted spoon, to allow draining, or with a ladle into small side-dish bowls.
